title: Frazeologizmlar va maqollar
goal_uz: Dars oxirida 12 ta inglizcha maqolni o‘zbekcha (yoki ruscha) muqobili bilan bog‘laysiz, 15 dan ortiq turg‘un iborani (idiom, binomial, o‘xshatish) shaklini buzmasdan ishlatasiz, ularni vaziyat va registrga mos tanlaysiz hamda kamida 6 ta iboraning madaniy kelib chiqishini tushuntirib bera olasiz.

scenes.title: Xalq donoligi
board: Proverbs · Idioms · Set expressions
(Maqollar · Iboralar · Turg‘un birikmalar)
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda kinoya, kesatiq va inglizcha yumorni o‘rgandik: aytilgani bilan nazarda tutilgani farq qiladigan gaplarni. Bugun shunga yaqin, lekin boshqa hodisa: ma’nosi so‘zlardan emas, butun iboradan chiqadigan birikmalar. Dars oxirida maqollarni o‘zbekcha muqobili bilan bog‘laysiz, iboralarni shaklini buzmasdan ishlatasiz, ularni vaziyatga mos tanlaysiz va kelib chiqishini bilasiz.
scenes.say: A proverb is the wisdom of many and the wit of one. Today you'll learn to use that wisdom without sounding like a dictionary.
scenes.say_uz: Maqol — ko‘pchilikning donoligi va bir kishining zukkoligi. Bugun bu donolikdan lug‘atdek eshitilmasdan foydalanishni o‘rganasiz.

scenes.title: Maqol, ibora, birikma
board: Proverb = a complete sentence of advice
Idiom = a phrase with a figurative meaning
Set expression = fixed wording (salt and pepper)

examples.t: Strike while the iron is hot.
examples.uz: Temirni qizig‘ida bos. (maqol)

examples.t: She's under the weather.
examples.uz: Uning tobi yo‘q. (ibora)

examples.t: sooner or later
examples.uz: ertami-kechmi (turg‘un birikma)

scenes.say_native: Uch tushunchani farqlaymiz. Proverb, ya’ni maqol — maslahat yoki hayotiy xulosa beruvchi to‘liq gap. Idiom — ma’nosi tarkibidagi so‘zlardan kelib chiqmaydigan ibora: “under the weather” ob-havo ostida emas, “tobi yo‘q” degani. Set expression esa so‘zlari va tartibi qotib qolgan birikma: “sooner or later”, hech qachon “later or sooner” emas. O‘zbek tilida ham shu uchala qatlam bor.
scenes.say: Proverbs give advice, idioms paint pictures, and set expressions simply refuse to change their shape.
scenes.say_uz: Maqollar maslahat beradi, iboralar tasvir chizadi, turg‘un birikmalar esa shaklini o‘zgartirishni rad etadi.

scenes.title: To‘liq muqobillar
board: Strike while the iron is hot. = Temirni qizig‘ida bos.
Measure twice, cut once. ≈ Yetti o‘lchab, bir kes.
Out of sight, out of mind. = Ko‘zdan yiroq — ko‘ngildan yiroq.

examples.t: They've offered you the job; strike while the iron is hot.
examples.uz: Sizga ishni taklif qilishdi, temirni qizig‘ida bosing.

examples.t: Measure twice, cut once: check the contract again.
examples.uz: Yetti o‘lchab, bir kesing: shartnomani yana tekshiring.

scenes.say_native: Yaxshi xabar: ko‘p maqollar ikki tilda deyarli bir xil. “Strike while the iron is hot” — aynan “Temirni qizig‘ida bos”. “Out of sight, out of mind” — “Ko‘zdan yiroq — ko‘ngildan yiroq”. Ba’zan faqat raqam farq qiladi: biz yetti marta o‘lchaymiz, inglizlar ikki marta. Bunday maqollar xavfsiz: tasvir va ma’no bir xil, faqat inglizcha shaklini aniq yodlash kerak.
scenes.say: Some proverbs travel well. The blacksmith's advice about hot iron works in English, Uzbek, Russian and dozens of other languages.
scenes.say_uz: Ba’zi maqollar yaxshi “sayohat qiladi”. Temirchining qizigan temir haqidagi maslahati ingliz, o‘zbek, rus va o‘nlab boshqa tillarda ishlaydi.

scenes.title: Bir ma’no, boshqa tasvir
board: Don't count your chickens before they're hatched. ≈ Jo‘jani kuzda sanaydilar.
The grass is always greener on the other side. ≈ Qo‘shnining tovug‘i g‘oz ko‘rinar.
Birds of a feather flock together. ≈ Kaptar kaptar bilan, lochin lochin bilan.

examples.t: Don't count your chickens; the deal isn't signed yet.
examples.uz: Jo‘jani kuzda sanaydilar: bitim hali imzolanmagan.

examples.t: He thinks every other job is better. The grass is always greener.
examples.uz: Unga har qanday boshqa ish yaxshiroq ko‘rinadi. Qo‘shnining tovug‘i g‘oz ko‘rinar.

scenes.say_native: Ko‘p hollarda ma’no bir xil, tasvir esa boshqa. Ikkala tilda ham jo‘ja bor, lekin inglizlar “tuxumdan chiqmasdan sanama” deydi, biz “kuzda sanaymiz”. Inglizlarda qo‘shnining o‘ti yashilroq, bizda qo‘shnining tovug‘i g‘oz ko‘rinadi. Qushlar haqidagi maqolda ham ikki tilda qushlar bor. Bunday juftlarni tanib olish — darajangiz yuqori ekanining belgisi.
scenes.say: Same wisdom, different farmyard. The English worry about eggs that haven't hatched; Uzbeks wait until autumn to count the chicks.
scenes.say_uz: Bir xil donolik, boshqa hovli. Inglizlar hali chiqmagan tuxumlar haqida qayg‘uradi, o‘zbeklar esa jo‘jani sanash uchun kuzni kutadi.

scenes.title: Yana muqobillar
board: Little by little / Every little helps. ≈ Tomchi-tomchi ko‘l bo‘lur.
When in Rome, do as the Romans do. ≈ Qaysi elga borsang, o‘sha elning qalpog‘ini kiy.
The apple doesn't fall far from the tree. ≈ Qush uyasida ko‘rganini qiladi.

examples.t: Save a little every month. Every little helps.
examples.uz: Har oy ozgina jamg‘aring. Tomchi-tomchi ko‘l bo‘lur.

examples.t: He's a doctor like his father. The apple doesn't fall far from the tree.
examples.uz: U otasi kabi shifokor. Qush uyasida ko‘rganini qiladi.

scenes.say_native: Yana uchta foydali juftlik. “Every little helps” — Britaniyada juda keng ishlatiladi, bizning “Tomchi-tomchi ko‘l bo‘lur”ga to‘g‘ri keladi. “When in Rome, do as the Romans do” — “Qaysi elga borsang, o‘sha elning qalpog‘ini kiy”. “The apple doesn't fall far from the tree” — farzand ota-onasiga o‘xshaydi; o‘zbekchada “Qush uyasida ko‘rganini qiladi” deymiz. Rus tilini bilsangiz, “Яблоко от яблони недалеко падает” ham xuddi shu tasvir.
scenes.say: When in Rome, do as the Romans do. Or, as an Uzbek might put it, when you visit another land, wear its hat.
scenes.say_uz: Rimda bo‘lsang, rimliklar kabi yo‘l tut. Yoki o‘zbekcha aytganda, qaysi elga borsang, o‘sha elning qalpog‘ini kiy.

scenes.title: Muqobili yo‘q maqollar
board: A rolling stone gathers no moss. (2 interpretations)
Curiosity killed the cat. (= don't be too nosy)
Explain the meaning, don't force an equivalent

examples.t: Curiosity killed the cat, so stop reading my messages.
examples.uz: Ortiqcha qiziquvchanlik boshga balo, xabarlarimni o‘qishni bas qil.

scenes.say_native: Ba’zi maqollarning aniq muqobili yo‘q yoki ma’nosi bahsli. “A rolling stone gathers no moss” an’anaviy talqinda salbiy: bir joyda turmagan odam boylik orttirmaydi. Hozir ba’zilar uni ijobiy ma’noda ham ishlatadi: harakatdagi odam eskirmaydi. Shuning uchun kontekstga qarang. “Curiosity killed the cat” — “ortiqcha qiziqma”. Bunday hollarda o‘zbekchaga majburan muqobil qidirmang, ma’nosini tushuntiring.
scenes.say: A rolling stone gathers no moss. For some, that's a warning against restlessness; for others, it's a reason to keep moving.
scenes.say_uz: Dumalayotgan tosh mox bosmaydi. Ba’zilar uchun bu beqarorlikka qarshi ogohlantirish, boshqalar uchun esa harakatda qolish uchun sabab.

scenes.title: So‘zma-so‘z tarjima qilingan maqol
board: ✗ Chickens are counted in autumn.
✓ Don't count your chickens before they're hatched.
✗ Measure seven times, cut once. (calque)
✓ Measure twice, cut once.
scenes.say_native: Eng tipik xato — o‘zbekcha maqolni so‘zma-so‘z tarjima qilib, ingliz suhbatdoshidan tushunishni kutish. “Chickens are counted in autumn” ingliz quloqqa g‘alati eshitiladi. Agar o‘zbek maqolini ataylab keltirmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, buni ochiq ayting: “As we say in Uzbek, …”, keyin inglizcha muqobilni qo‘shing. Shunda tarjimangiz xato emas, madaniy boylik bo‘lib eshitiladi.
scenes.say: If you want to share an Uzbek proverb, flag it: 'As we say in Uzbek, chickens are counted in autumn.' Then it sounds charming, not wrong.
scenes.say_uz: O‘zbek maqolini aytmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, belgilab qo‘ying: “O‘zbekcha aytganda, jo‘jani kuzda sanaydilar.” Shunda u xato emas, yoqimli eshitiladi.

scenes.title: Muqobilini toping
board: 1 Out of sight, out of mind.
2 The grass is always greener on the other side.
3 When in Rome, do as the Romans do.
4 Strike while the iron is hot.
scenes.say_native: Endi esingizda qolganini tekshiramiz. Ekrandagi to‘rtta inglizcha maqol uchun o‘zbekcha muqobilni ayting. Agar o‘zbekchasini eslay olmasangiz, ma’nosini o‘z so‘zlaringiz bilan tushuntiring. Keyin har biri uchun hayotiy vaziyat o‘ylab ko‘ring: bu maqolni qachon ishlatgan bo‘lardingiz?
scenes.say: Give the Uzbek equivalent of each proverb, and think of a moment in your own life when you could use it.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir maqolning o‘zbekcha muqobilini ayting va uni o‘z hayotingizda qachon ishlata olishingizni o‘ylang.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Ko‘zdan yiroq — ko‘ngildan yiroq.
2 Qo‘shnining tovug‘i g‘oz ko‘rinar.
3 Qaysi elga borsang, o‘sha elning qalpog‘ini kiy.
4 Temirni qizig‘ida bos.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: birinchisi — “Ko‘zdan yiroq — ko‘ngildan yiroq”, masalan, uzoqqa ketgan do‘st bilan aloqa susayganda. Ikkinchisi — “Qo‘shnining tovug‘i g‘oz ko‘rinar”, boshqalarning hayoti yaxshiroq tuyulganda. Uchinchisi — “Qaysi elga borsang, o‘sha elning qalpog‘ini kiy”, chet elda mahalliy odatga moslashganda. To‘rtinchisi — “Temirni qizig‘ida bos”, imkoniyat qo‘ldan ketmasdan harakat qilganda.
scenes.say: Notice that in English, people often quote only the first half: 'Well, when in Rome…' Everyone completes the rest in their head.
scenes.say_uz: E’tibor bering, ingliz tilida ko‘pincha faqat birinchi yarmi aytiladi: “Xo‘sh, Rimda bo‘lsang…” Qolganini hamma xayolan to‘ldiradi.

scenes.title: Kundalik iboralar
board: a piece of cake (juda oson) · under the weather (tobi yo‘q)
cost an arm and a leg (juda qimmat)
break the ice · spill the beans · the ball is in your court

examples.t: The exam was a piece of cake.
examples.uz: Imtihon juda oson bo‘ldi.

examples.t: Who spilled the beans about the party?
examples.uz: Ziyofat haqidagi sirni kim oshkor qildi?

examples.t: I've made my offer; the ball is in your court.
examples.uz: Taklifimni berdim, endi navbat sizda.

scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi mavzu — turg‘un iboralar. Eng ko‘p ishlatiladiganlari: “a piece of cake” — juda oson; “under the weather” — tobi yo‘q; “cost an arm and a leg” — juda qimmat; “break the ice” — tanishuvdagi noqulaylikni yo‘qotmoq; “spill the beans” — sirni oshkor qilmoq; “the ball is in your court” — endi qaror sizda.
scenes.say: The new flat cost an arm and a leg, so when my friend asked me to lend her money, I had to break it to her gently.
scenes.say_uz: Yangi kvartira juda qimmatga tushdi, shuning uchun dugonam qarz so‘raganida, unga buni muloyimlik bilan aytishimga to‘g‘ri keldi.

scenes.title: Juft iboralar: binomials
board: salt and pepper · black and white · sooner or later
by and large · odds and ends · safe and sound
pros and cons · peace and quiet · now and then

examples.t: By and large, the trip went well.
examples.uz: Umuman olganda, safar yaxshi o‘tdi.

examples.t: They arrived home safe and sound.
examples.uz: Ular uyga sog‘-salomat yetib kelishdi.

scenes.say_native: Binomial — “and” yoki “or” bilan bog‘langan, tartibi qotib qolgan juftlik. “Salt and pepper”, “black and white”, “safe and sound”, “peace and quiet”. Tartibni almashtirsangiz, ma’no o‘zgarmasa ham, eshitilishi g‘alati bo‘ladi: “pepper and salt” deyilmaydi. O‘zbekchada ham shunday: “ota-ona”, “oq-qora”, “katta-kichik”, hech kim “ona-ota” demaydi. Har bir binomialni bir butun so‘z sifatida yodlang.
scenes.say: Binomials are like old married couples: they always appear together, and always in the same order.
scenes.say_uz: Binomiallar keksa er-xotinga o‘xshaydi: doim birga va doim bir xil tartibda ko‘rinadi.

scenes.title: Turg‘un o‘xshatishlar
board: as cool as a cucumber (juda xotirjam)
as fit as a fiddle (sog‘-salomat, baquvvat)
as old as the hills · as good as gold (juda odobli)

examples.t: Before the interview she was as cool as a cucumber.
examples.uz: Suhbatdan oldin u mutlaqo xotirjam edi.

examples.t: My grandfather is ninety and as fit as a fiddle.
examples.uz: Bobom to‘qsonda, lekin qayrag‘ochdek baquvvat.

scenes.say_native: Inglizcha o‘xshatishlar “as … as …” qolipida bo‘ladi va ko‘pincha mantiqiy emas, an’anaviy. Nega bodring xotirjam, skripka esa sog‘lom? Bu tarixiy tasodif, mantiq qidirmang. O‘zbekchada ham “qayrag‘ochdek”, “tulkidek ayyor” deymiz. Ba’zi tasvirlar mos tushadi: “as sly as a fox” — “tulkidek ayyor”. Ba’zilari farq qiladi, shuning uchun har birini alohida yodlang.
scenes.say: Why is a cucumber cool and a fiddle fit? Nobody really knows, and nobody really cares. You simply learn them as they are.
scenes.say_uz: Nega bodring xotirjam, skripka esa sog‘lom? Buni hech kim aniq bilmaydi va hech kimga qiziq emas. Siz ularni boricha o‘rganasiz.

scenes.title: Iboralarning grammatikasi
board: Tense changes: She spilled the beans.
Pronoun changes: pull your / his / their weight
Frozen: kick the bucket (✗ The bucket was kicked.)

examples.t: Everyone has to pull their weight.
examples.uz: Har kim o‘z ulushini bajarishi kerak.

examples.t: Once the ice had been broken, the talks went smoothly.
examples.uz: Noqulaylik yo‘qolgach, muzokaralar silliq ketdi.

scenes.say_native: Iboralar grammatik jihatdan qanchalik egiluvchan? Zamon deyarli har doim o‘zgaradi: “spills the beans”, “spilled the beans”. Olmosh egasiga moslashadi: “pull your weight”, “pull their weight”. Ba’zi iboralar majhul nisbatga ham o‘ta oladi: “once the ice had been broken”. Lekin “kick the bucket”, ya’ni “olamdan o‘tmoq”, butunlay qotgan: “the bucket was kicked” desangiz, idiom ma’nosi yo‘qoladi.
scenes.say: Some idioms bend; others break. 'The ice was broken' still works, but 'the bucket was kicked' only means that someone kicked a bucket.
scenes.say_uz: Ba’zi iboralar egiladi, ba’zilari sinadi. “Muz sindirildi” hamon ishlaydi, “paqir tepildi” esa faqat kimdir paqirni tepganini anglatadi.

scenes.title: Buzilgan iboralar
board: ✗ It cost an arm and leg. → ✓ an arm and a leg
✗ pepper and salt → ✓ salt and pepper
✗ He spilled beans. → ✓ He spilled the beans.
✗ It's a cake piece. → ✓ It's a piece of cake.
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida so‘zlashuvchilarda eng ko‘p uchraydigan xato — artiklni tushirib qoldirish, chunki o‘zbek tilida artikl yo‘q. “An arm and a leg”da ikkala artikl ham shart, “spill the beans”da “the” shart. Ikkinchi xato — so‘z tartibini o‘zgartirish. Uchinchisi — sinonim bilan almashtirish: “a piece of pie” yoki “spill the peas” deyilmaydi. Iborada har bir so‘z, hatto artikl ham, o‘z joyida turadi.
scenes.say: An idiom is a key, not a sentence. Change one tooth, even a tiny article, and it no longer opens the door.
scenes.say_uz: Ibora gap emas, kalit. Bitta tishini, hatto kichkina artiklni o‘zgartirsangiz, u endi eshikni ochmaydi.

scenes.title: Iborani to‘ldiring
board: 1 Don't worry, the test will be a piece of …
2 I'm feeling a bit under the … today.
3 Sooner or … you'll have to tell her.
4 They got home safe and …
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta iborani to‘ldiring. Har birida bitta so‘z yetishmaydi. Javobni artikl va so‘z tartibi bilan to‘liq, ovoz chiqarib ayting, chunki iborada har bir kichik so‘z muhim. So‘ng har bir iboraning o‘zbekcha ma’nosini ham ayting, shunda ham shaklini, ham mazmunini bir vaqtda mustahkamlaysiz.
scenes.say: Complete each expression, then say what it means in Uzbek.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir iborani to‘ldiring, so‘ng o‘zbekcha nimani anglatishini ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 cake (juda oson)
2 weather (tobi yo‘q)
3 later (ertami-kechmi)
4 sound (sog‘-salomat)
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: “a piece of cake” — juda oson; “under the weather” — tobi yo‘q, biroz kasal; “sooner or later” — ertami-kechmi; “safe and sound” — sog‘-salomat. E’tibor bering, “under the weather” jiddiy kasallik uchun emas, yengil holsizlik uchun ishlatiladi. Kasalxonada yotgan odam haqida bunday deyish ko‘pincha noo‘rin bo‘ladi.
scenes.say: 'Under the weather' means slightly unwell. If someone has broken their leg, they're not under the weather; they're in hospital.
scenes.say_uz: “Under the weather” — biroz tobi yo‘q degani. Kimdir oyog‘ini sindirgan bo‘lsa, uning shunchaki tobi yo‘q emas, u kasalxonada.

scenes.title: Tinglash: muhim uchrashuvdan keyin
board: Dan & Sara, after a client meeting
Listen for: 6 idioms
scenes.say_native: Birinchi dialogni tinglang. Sara mijoz bilan muhim uchrashuvdan qaytdi, hamkasbi Dan natijani so‘rayapti. Dialogda kamida oltita ibora bor. Ularni sanab boring va har birining ma’nosini kontekstdan topishga harakat qiling. Keyin savollarga javob berasiz.
scenes.say: Dan: So, how did the pitch go? Sara: Honestly, it was a piece of cake, once we'd broken the ice. Dan: And the budget? Sara: That's the catch. Their new system will cost an arm and a leg. Dan: So the ball's in their court now. Sara: Exactly. But don't spill the beans to the team yet. Nothing's set in stone. Dan: My lips are sealed.
scenes.say_uz: Dan: Xo‘sh, taqdimot qanday o‘tdi? Sara: Rostini aytsam, juda oson bo‘ldi, noqulaylikni yengganimizdan keyin. Dan: Budjet-chi? Sara: Gap shunda. Ularning yangi tizimi juda qimmatga tushadi. Dan: Demak, endi navbat ularda. Sara: Aynan. Lekin jamoaga hozircha sirni aytma. Hech narsa qat’iy emas. Dan: Og‘zim mahkam.

scenes.title: Dialog bo‘yicha savollar
board: 1 How difficult was the pitch?
2 What is 'the catch'?
3 Who has to decide next?
4 What does Sara ask Dan to do, and why?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savolga inglizcha qisqa javob bering. Taqdimot qanchalik qiyin bo‘ldi? “The catch”, ya’ni muammo nima? Endi kim qaror qilishi kerak? Sara Danga nima qilishni aytdi va nima uchun? Javob berishda iboralarning o‘zini takrorlamang, ularni oddiy so‘zlar bilan ochib bering: bu ma’nosini tushunganingizni ko‘rsatadi.
scenes.say: Answer in plain English, without using the idioms themselves.
scenes.say_uz: Iboralarning o‘zini ishlatmasdan, oddiy ingliz tilida javob bering.

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
board: 1 Easy, after an awkward start
2 The system is very expensive.
3 The client
4 Keep it secret: nothing is final.
scenes.say_native: Taqdimot oson bo‘ldi, lekin boshida biroz noqulaylik bor edi: “once we'd broken the ice”. Muammo — narx: “cost an arm and a leg”. Endi mijoz qaror qiladi: “the ball's in their court”. Sara sirni hozircha jamoaga aytmaslikni so‘radi, chunki hech narsa qat’iy emas: “set in stone”, ya’ni toshga o‘yilgan, o‘zgarmas. “My lips are sealed” — “og‘zim mahkam, hech kimga aytmayman”.
scenes.say: Six idioms in under thirty seconds. That's natural in casual office talk, but it would be far too many in a written report.
scenes.say_uz: O‘ttiz soniyadan kam vaqtda oltita ibora. Norasmiy ofis suhbatida bu tabiiy, lekin yozma hisobotda bu juda ko‘p bo‘lardi.

scenes.title: Registr: qachon mos?
board: Idioms: conversation, emails to colleagues, journalism
Avoid: academic essays, legal texts, formal reports
Proverbs: advice, speeches, wry comments

examples.t: ✗ The results were a piece of cake to interpret.
examples.uz: Natijalarni talqin qilish juda oson edi. (ilmiy matnda noo‘rin)

examples.t: ✓ The results were straightforward to interpret.
examples.uz: Natijalarni talqin qilish oson edi. (ilmiy uslub)

scenes.say_native: Uchinchi mavzu — iborani joyida ishlatish. Ko‘p iboralar norasmiy yoki neytral: suhbatda, hamkasbga xatda, publitsistikada tabiiy. Ilmiy maqola, huquqiy hujjat va rasmiy hisobotda esa ulardan qoching, o‘rniga aniq so‘z ishlating: “a piece of cake” emas, “straightforward”. Maqollar maslahat berishda, nutqda yoki kinoyali izohda yaxshi ishlaydi.
scenes.say: In a seminar, 'the data are straightforward' sounds scholarly; 'the data are a piece of cake' sounds like a student who stayed up too late.
scenes.say_uz: Seminarda “ma’lumotlar oddiy” ilmiy eshitiladi, “ma’lumotlar juda oson, bir chimdim” esa tunni bedor o‘tkazgan talabaning gapiga o‘xshaydi.

scenes.title: Yarim aytilgan maqollar
board: Speak of the devil… (and he shall appear)
Birds of a feather… · When in Rome…
If the shoe fits… (US) / If the cap fits… (UK)

examples.t: Speak of the devil! We were just talking about you.
examples.uz: Bo‘ri haqida gapirsang, qulog‘i ko‘rinadi! Hozirgina sen haqingda gaplashayotgan edik.

examples.t: I'm not naming names, but if the cap fits…
examples.uz: Ism aytmayman, lekin kimga tegishli bo‘lsa, o‘zi tushunar…

scenes.say_native: Ona tilida so‘zlashuvchilar mashhur maqolni ko‘pincha yarmigacha aytadi: “Speak of the devil…”, “Birds of a feather…”. Qolganini tinglovchi o‘zi to‘ldiradi. Bu tabiiy va nozik eshitiladi, to‘liq maqol esa ba’zan o‘qituvchinikiday tuyuladi. “Speak of the devil” o‘zbekchadagi “Bo‘ri haqida gapirsang, qulog‘i ko‘rinadi”ga juda yaqin. “If the cap fits” britancha, amerikada “if the shoe fits”.
scenes.say: Natives rarely finish a famous proverb. Say 'speak of the devil' as your friend walks in, and that's all you need.
scenes.say_uz: Ona tili egalari mashhur maqolni kamdan-kam oxiriga yetkazadi. Do‘stingiz kirib kelganda “speak of the devil” deng, shuning o‘zi yetarli.

scenes.title: Eskirgan iboralar va klishelar
board: Rare in real speech: It's raining cats and dogs.
More natural (UK): It's pouring. · It's chucking it down.
Clichés: at the end of the day · think outside the box

examples.t: Take a brolly, it's chucking it down.
examples.uz: Soyabon ol, sharillab yog‘yapti. (britancha so‘zlashuv)

scenes.say_native: Darsliklarda mashhur bo‘lgan ba’zi iboralar haqiqiy nutqda kam uchraydi. “It's raining cats and dogs”ni o‘quvchilar ko‘p ishlatadi, ona tili egalari esa ko‘pincha “it's pouring” yoki britancha so‘zlashuvda “it's chucking it down” deydi. Klishe ham xavfli: “at the end of the day”, “think outside the box” kabi ofis iboralari haddan ortiq ishlatilgani uchun ko‘pincha masxara qilinadi. C2 darajasida iborani tanlash — tirik va eskirganini farqlash demakdir.
scenes.say: Nothing marks a learner more clearly than a textbook idiom no one has used since the nineteen-fifties.
scenes.say_uz: O‘quvchini darslikdagi, 1950-yillardan beri hech kim ishlatmagan iboradek hech narsa aniq fosh qilmaydi.

scenes.title: Noo‘rin maqol
board: ✗ (at a funeral) Every cloud has a silver lining.
✓ I'm so sorry for your loss.
✗ Five idioms in one sentence
✓ One idiom, well placed
scenes.say_native: Maqol ba’zan juda noo‘rin bo‘lishi mumkin. Motam marosimida “Every cloud has a silver lining”, ya’ni “har yomonlikning yaxshi tomoni bor” deyish qo‘pollik. Og‘ir vaziyatda oddiy, samimiy gap kerak: “I'm so sorry for your loss.” Ikkinchi xato — iboralarni tizib tashlash. Bir jumlada beshta ibora kulgili, hatto parodiyadek eshitiladi. Qoida: bitta ibora, to‘g‘ri joyda.
scenes.say: A proverb in the wrong moment sounds cold, as if you've reached for a ready-made answer instead of listening.
scenes.say_uz: Noto‘g‘ri paytdagi maqol sovuq eshitiladi, go‘yo siz tinglash o‘rniga tayyor javobga qo‘l cho‘zgandek.

scenes.title: Mosmi yoki yo‘q?
board: 1 Dissertation: 'This theory is as old as the hills.'
2 To a friend who failed a test: 'Every cloud has a silver lining.'
3 Friend walks in: 'Speak of the devil!'
4 Email to a new client: 'Your offer costs an arm and a leg.'
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta vaziyat. Har birida ibora yoki maqol mosmi, noo‘rinmi, aniqlang. Noo‘rin bo‘lsa, uning o‘rniga nima deyish yaxshiroq ekanini o‘ylang. Vaziyatning rasmiyligi, suhbatdoshning kayfiyati va matn turini hisobga oling. Ikkinchisida o‘ylab ko‘ring: bu yengil vaziyatmi yoki og‘irmi?
scenes.say: Appropriate or not? If not, suggest something better.
scenes.say_uz: Mosmi yoki yo‘qmi? Mos bo‘lmasa, yaxshiroq variant taklif qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 ✗ → This theory dates back to the 1890s.
2 ✓ (a minor setback, said kindly)
3 ✓ Natural and friendly
4 ✗ → The price is higher than we anticipated.
scenes.say_native: Birinchisi noo‘rin: dissertatsiyada ibora o‘rniga aniq ma’lumot kerak, masalan, “dates back to the 1890s”. Ikkinchisi mos: test — kichik muvaffaqiyatsizlik, maqol iliq ohangda aytilsa, dalda beradi. Motamdan farqi shu. Uchinchisi mutlaqo tabiiy. To‘rtinchisi noo‘rin: yangi mijozga xatda norasmiy ibora qo‘pol eshitiladi, “higher than we anticipated” — muloyim va aniq.
scenes.say: The same proverb can comfort or wound. The difference is the size of the problem and the closeness of the relationship.
scenes.say_uz: Bir maqol ham taskin berishi, ham yaralashi mumkin. Farq muammoning kattaligi va munosabatning yaqinligida.

scenes.title: Madaniy ildizlar: Injil
board: the writing on the wall (Daniel) = a sign of coming disaster
a wolf in sheep's clothing (Matthew) = a hidden enemy
the salt of the earth (Matthew) = a good, honest person

examples.t: When sales fell for the third year, the writing was on the wall.
examples.uz: Savdo uchinchi yil tushganda, oqibati aniq ko‘rinib qolgan edi.

examples.t: My neighbours are the salt of the earth.
examples.uz: Qo‘shnilarim juda oddiy va halol odamlar.

scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi mavzu — madaniy kelib chiqish. Ko‘p inglizcha iboralar Injildan, ayniqsa uning 1611-yilgi King James tarjimasi orqali tilga singgan. “The writing on the wall” — Doniyor kitobidagi devorga yozilgan sirli so‘zlar haqidagi hikoyadan, “yaqinlashayotgan falokat belgisi”. “A wolf in sheep's clothing” — “qo‘y terisiga o‘ralgan bo‘ri”, bizda ham shu tasvir bor. “The salt of the earth” — “halol, oddiy, yaxshi odam”.
scenes.say: You don't need to be religious to use these expressions, but knowing the stories behind them helps you feel their weight.
scenes.say_uz: Bu iboralarni ishlatish uchun dindor bo‘lish shart emas, lekin ularning ortidagi hikoyalarni bilish salmog‘ini his qilishga yordam beradi.

scenes.title: Madaniy ildizlar: Shekspir
board: the green-eyed monster (Othello) = jealousy
a wild-goose chase (Romeo and Juliet) = a pointless search
vanish into thin air (cf. The Tempest) = disappear completely

examples.t: Looking for that file was a wild-goose chase.
examples.uz: U faylni qidirish behuda ovora bo‘lish edi.

examples.t: Beware the green-eyed monster.
examples.uz: Hasaddan ehtiyot bo‘ling.

scenes.say_native: Shekspir asarlari ham ingliz tiliga ko‘plab iboralar bergan yoki ularni ommalashtirgan. “The green-eyed monster” — “Otello” pyesasidagi hasad timsoli. “A wild-goose chase” — “Romeo va Julyetta”da uchraydi, bugun “behuda qidiruv, ovoragarchilik” ma’nosida. “Into thin air” — “Bo‘ron” pyesasidagi satrga borib taqaladi. Inglizlar bularni Shekspirdan ekanini bilmasdan ham ishlatadi, xuddi biz Navoiydan kelgan iboralarni ishlatganimizdek.
scenes.say: Every time you call jealousy 'the green-eyed monster', you are quoting Othello, whether you know it or not.
scenes.say_uz: Har safar hasadni “yashil ko‘zli maxluq” deb ataganingizda, bilasizmi-yo‘qmi, “Otello”dan iqtibos keltirasiz.

scenes.title: Orol xalqi: dengiz iboralari
board: learn the ropes (ishning ko‘zini o‘rganmoq)
taken aback (hayron qolgan) · by and large
show your true colours (asl qiyofasini ko‘rsatmoq)

examples.t: It took me a month to learn the ropes.
examples.uz: Ishning ko‘zini o‘rganishimga bir oy ketdi.

examples.t: I was taken aback by his reply.
examples.uz: Uning javobidan hayron qoldim.

scenes.say_native: Britaniya — orol, uning tarixi dengiz bilan bog‘liq, shuning uchun ko‘p iboralar yelkanli kemalardan kelgan. “Learn the ropes” — dastlab arqonlarni bilishni o‘rganish, endi “ishning ko‘zini o‘rganmoq”. “Taken aback” — shamol yelkanni orqaga bosgan holat, endi “hayratda qolmoq”. “Show your true colours” — kemaning asl bayrog‘ini ko‘rsatish. O‘zbek iboralarida esa dasht, ot, non, qozon va karvon tasvirlari ko‘p: har xalq o‘z hayotidan tasvir oladi.
scenes.say: An island nation talks like sailors. A Silk Road nation talks about bread, horses and caravans. The idioms tell you where a people has lived.
scenes.say_uz: Orol xalqi dengizchilardek gapiradi. Ipak yo‘li xalqi non, ot va karvonlar haqida gapiradi. Iboralar xalq qayerda yashaganini aytib beradi.

scenes.title: Sport va ichimlik: UK va US
board: UK cricket: on a sticky wicket · hit for six
US baseball: a ballpark figure · touch base
UK: a storm in a teacup · US: a tempest in a teapot

examples.t: Can you give me a ballpark figure?
examples.uz: Taxminiy raqamni ayta olasizmi?

examples.t: The news really hit me for six.
examples.uz: Bu xabar meni butunlay esankiratib qo‘ydi.

scenes.say_native: Sport iboralari Britaniya bilan Amerikani ajratadi. Britaniyada kriket: “on a sticky wicket” — qiyin ahvolda; “hit for six” — esankiratib qo‘ymoq. Amerikada beysbol: “a ballpark figure” — taxminiy raqam; “touch base” — qisqa bog‘lanmoq. Choy ham farq qiladi: britancha “a storm in a teacup”, amerikacha “a tempest in a teapot”, ikkalasi ham “arzimas narsa uchun shov-shuv”. Amerikalik suhbatdoshga kriket iborasi tushunarsiz bo‘lishi mumkin.
scenes.say: If you tell an American colleague you're on a sticky wicket, don't be surprised by a blank look. Cricket idioms rarely cross the Atlantic.
scenes.say_uz: Amerikalik hamkasbga “sticky wicket”dasiz desangiz, hayron nigohdan ajablanmang. Kriket iboralari Atlantikani kamdan-kam kesib o‘tadi.

scenes.title: Aralash iboralar
board: ✗ It's not my cup of coffee. → ✓ not my cup of tea
✗ a storm in a teapot → ✓ a storm in a teacup (UK)
✗ We'll cross that bridge when we burn it.
✓ We'll cross that bridge when we come to it.
scenes.say_native: Yana bir keng tarqalgan xato — ikki iborani aralashtirish, inglizcha “mixed idiom”. “A storm in a teapot” — britancha va amerikacha shakllarning qo‘shilishi. “Cross that bridge when we burn it” esa ikki iboradan yasalgan: “cross that bridge when we come to it”, ya’ni “muammoga duch kelganda hal qilamiz”, va “burn your bridges”, ya’ni “orqaga yo‘lni yopmoq”. “Not my cup of tea” — “menga yoqmaydi”, choy o‘rniga qahva qo‘yilmaydi.
scenes.say: Mixed idioms sometimes appear in jokes on purpose. When they appear by accident, the joke is on you.
scenes.say_uz: Aralash iboralar ba’zan hazilda ataylab ishlatiladi. Tasodifan chiqib qolsa, kulgi sizning ustingizdan bo‘ladi.

scenes.title: Kelib chiqishini toping
board: 1 learn the ropes
2 the writing on the wall
3 a ballpark figure
4 the green-eyed monster
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta ibora uchun manbani toping: dengizchilik, Injil, Amerika sporti yoki Shekspir. So‘ng har birining zamonaviy ma’nosini bitta inglizcha jumla bilan ayting. Manbani bilish iborani to‘g‘ri vaziyatda ishlatishga yordam beradi: masalan, Amerikadan kelgan ibora amerikalik suhbatdoshga yaqinroq.
scenes.say: Sailing, the Bible, American sport or Shakespeare? Match each idiom to its source and give its modern meaning.
scenes.say_uz: Dengizchilik, Injil, Amerika sporti yoki Shekspir? Har bir iborani manbasiga moslang va zamonaviy ma’nosini ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar
board: 1 Sailing → learn how a job works
2 The Bible → a sign of coming trouble
3 Baseball (US) → a rough estimate
4 Shakespeare → jealousy
scenes.say_native: Birinchisi dengizchilikdan: yangi ishning ko‘zini o‘rganmoq. Ikkinchisi Injildan, Doniyor kitobidan: yaqinlashayotgan falokat belgisi. Uchinchisi Amerika beysbolidan: taxminiy hisob, “roughly how much?” savoliga javob. To‘rtinchisi Shekspirning “Otello” asaridan: hasad. Endi bu iboralarni eshitganingizda, ularning ortidagi tasvirni ham ko‘rasiz.
scenes.say: Learn the ropes, read the writing on the wall, give a ballpark figure, and beware the green-eyed monster. Four sources, one language.
scenes.say_uz: Ishning ko‘zini o‘rganing, ogohlantiruvchi belgini ko‘ring, taxminiy raqam bering va hasaddan ehtiyot bo‘ling. To‘rtta manba, bitta til.

scenes.title: Tinglash: maqollar suhbati
board: Malika (from Tashkent) & Jack (from Leeds)
Listen for: Uzbek proverbs and their English equivalents
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog. Toshkentlik Malika va Lidslik hamkasbi Jack choy ustida suhbatlashyapti. Malika singlisi haqida qayg‘urayotgan ekan va o‘zbek maqollarini inglizchaga o‘giradi. Jack ularning inglizcha muqobilini topadi. Diqqat bilan tinglang: qaysi maqollar aynan mos, qaysilari biroz farq qiladi?
scenes.say: Jack: You look worried, Malika. Malika: My sister wants to sell her flat before she's even found a new one. As we say in Uzbek, chickens are counted in autumn. Jack: Ah, don't count your chickens before they're hatched. Same idea, different season. Malika: And my mum always says: measure seven times, cut once. Jack: We only measure twice. Clearly we're less careful. Malika: Or just faster. Jack: Your mum and my gran would get on like a house on fire. Malika: Birds of a feather, as you say.
scenes.say_uz: Jack: Xavotirdasiz, Malika. Malika: Singlim yangi uy topmasdan turib kvartirasini sotmoqchi. O‘zbekchada aytganidek, jo‘jani kuzda sanaydilar. Jack: Ha, tuxumdan chiqmagan jo‘jani sanama. Bir g‘oya, boshqa fasl. Malika: Onam esa doim aytadi: yetti o‘lchab, bir kes. Jack: Biz faqat ikki marta o‘lchaymiz. Ko‘rinib turibdiki, biz kamroq ehtiyotkormiz. Malika: Yoki shunchaki tezroq. Jack: Onangiz bilan buvim juda tez til topishardi. Malika: Kaptar kaptar bilan, siz aytganingizdek.

scenes.title: Dialog bo‘yicha savollar
board: 1 What is Malika's sister planning to do?
2 How does Malika flag the Uzbek proverb?
3 How do the two 'measuring' proverbs differ?
4 What does 'get on like a house on fire' mean?
scenes.say_native: Dialog bo‘yicha to‘rtta savol. Malikaning singlisi nima qilmoqchi? Malika o‘zbek maqolini aytishdan oldin qaysi iborani ishlatdi? O‘lchash haqidagi ikki maqol nimasi bilan farq qiladi? Va oxirgi savol: “get on like a house on fire” iborasi nimani anglatadi? Ehtiyot bo‘ling, bu yerda yong‘in haqida gap yo‘q.
scenes.say: Four questions. Pay special attention to the last one: it's not about a fire at all.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta savol. Oxirgisiga alohida e’tibor bering: u umuman yong‘in haqida emas.

scenes.title: Dialog javoblari
board: 1 Sell her flat before finding a new one
2 'As we say in Uzbek, …'
3 Seven times vs twice
4 To like each other and get along very well
scenes.say_native: Singlisi yangi uy topmasdan eskisini sotmoqchi, shuning uchun “jo‘jani kuzda sanaydilar” mos keladi. Malika maqolni “As we say in Uzbek” bilan belgiladi: aynan biz o‘rgangan usul. O‘lchash maqollarida faqat raqam farq qiladi, Jack buni hazilga aylantirdi. “Get on like a house on fire” — “juda tez til topishmoq, apoq-chapoq bo‘lmoq”. Malika esa yarim maqol bilan javob berdi: “Birds of a feather”.
scenes.say: Malika finishes with half a proverb, just as a native speaker would. That's what fluency in idioms sounds like.
scenes.say_uz: Malika ona tili egasi kabi yarim maqol bilan yakunlaydi. Iboralarni erkin bilish shunday eshitiladi.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: urg‘u va bog‘lanish
board: Main stress on the last key word: a piece of CAKE
under the WEATHER · break the ICE
and → /ən/ or /n/: salt_and pepper, fish 'n' chips

examples.t: It was a piece of cake.
examples.uz: /ɪt wəz ə ˌpiːs əv ˈkeɪk/

examples.t: black and white
examples.uz: /ˌblæk ən ˈwaɪt/

scenes.say_native: Iboralar talaffuzida ikki qoida. Birinchisi: asosiy urg‘u odatda oxirgi mazmunli so‘zga tushadi: “a piece of CAKE”, “under the WEATHER”, “break the ICE”. Ikkinchisi: binomiallarda “and” kuchsiz shaklda /ən/ yoki hatto /n/ bo‘lib aytiladi va so‘zlar bog‘lanadi: “salt and pepper”, “fish and chips”. “Of” ham kuchsiz: /əv/.
scenes.say: Listen: a piece of cake. Fish and chips. Black and white. Safe and sound. The little words almost disappear, and the idiom flows as a single unit.
scenes.say_uz: Tinglang: a piece of cake. Fish and chips. Black and white. Safe and sound. Kichik so‘zlar deyarli yo‘qoladi va ibora bitta butun bo‘lib oqadi.

scenes.title: Ovoz chiqarib ayting
board: sooner or later · peace and quiet
It cost an arm and a leg.
The ball's in your court.
scenes.say_native: Endi ovoz chiqarib mashq qiling. Har bir iborani avval sekin, so‘ng tabiiy sur’atda ayting. Kichik so‘zlarni kuchsizlantiring: “or”, “and”, “a”, “the”. Asosiy urg‘uni oxirgi mazmunli so‘zga bering. Ikkinchi jumlada “arm and a leg” qanday bog‘lanishini sezishga harakat qiling.
scenes.say: Say each one slowly, then at natural speed. Let the little words shrink.
scenes.say_uz: Har birini avval sekin, keyin tabiiy sur’atda ayting. Kichik so‘zlarni qisqartiring.

scenes.title: Talaffuz namunasi
board: /ˌsuːnər ə ˈleɪtə/ · /ˌpiːs ən ˈkwaɪət/
an_arm_and_a LEG → /ən ˈɑːm ən ə ˈleg/
The ball's in your COURT.
scenes.say_native: Namunani tinglang. “Sooner or later”da “or” /ə/ bo‘lib qisqaradi. “Peace and quiet”da “and” deyarli eshitilmaydi. “An arm and a leg”da hamma so‘zlar bir zanjirga ulanadi: “an_arm_and_a leg”, urg‘u “arm” va “leg”ga tushadi, eng kuchlisi “leg”da. Oxirgi jumlada urg‘u “court”da. Agar sizniki shunga yaqin bo‘lsa, ibora tabiiy eshitiladi.
scenes.say: Sooner or later. Peace and quiet. It cost an arm and a leg. The ball's in your court.
scenes.say_uz: Ertami-kechmi. Tinchlik va osoyishtalik. Bu juda qimmatga tushdi. Endi navbat sizda.

scenes.title: Maqol bilan o‘ynash
board: Where there's a will, there's a way → … there's a lawsuit.
The early bird catches the worm, but the second mouse gets the cheese.
Twisted proverbs: headlines, ads, humour

examples.t: Where there's a will, there's a family argument.
examples.uz: Vasiyatnoma bor joyda oilaviy janjal bor. (will = iroda / vasiyatnoma)

scenes.say_native: C2 darajasida maqolni bilishgina emas, u bilan o‘ynay olish ham muhim. Gazeta sarlavhalari, reklama va hazilda mashhur maqol ataylab o‘zgartiriladi. “Where there's a will, there's a way” — “iroda bor joyda yo‘l bor”. “Will” vasiyatnoma ham bo‘lgani uchun hazilda “there's a lawsuit” yoki “a family argument” deyiladi. Bunday o‘yinni tushunish uchun asl maqolni bilish shart, shuning uchun avval asl shaklni puxta egallang.
scenes.say: The early bird catches the worm, but the second mouse gets the cheese. To enjoy the twist, you need to know the original.
scenes.say_uz: Erta turgan qush qurtni tutadi, lekin ikkinchi sichqon pishloqni oladi. O‘zgartirishdan zavq olish uchun asl maqolni bilish kerak.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq
board: Your friend wants to quit her job tomorrow
to start a business she hasn't planned yet.
Give advice using 3 proverbs or idioms.
scenes.say_native: Yakuniy ijodiy topshiriq. Dugonangiz ertaga ishdan ketib, hali rejalashtirilmagan biznes boshlamoqchi. Unga ingliz tilida qisqa maslahat bering: to‘rt-besh jumla, ichida kamida uchta maqol yoki ibora bo‘lsin. Bittasini yarmigacha aytib ko‘ring. Ohangni do‘stona saqlang va iboralarni tizib tashlamang, har biri o‘z o‘rnida bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: Give your friend some honest advice, using at least three proverbs or idioms naturally. One of them can be left half-finished.
scenes.say_uz: Dugonangizga kamida uchta maqol yoki iborani tabiiy ishlatib, samimiy maslahat bering. Ulardan birini yarmigacha aytishingiz mumkin.

scenes.title: Namunaviy javob
board: measure twice, cut once · don't burn your bridges
strike while the iron is hot
don't count your chickens…
scenes.say_native: Namunani tinglang. Unda to‘rtta ibora bor: “measure twice, cut once”, “burn your bridges”, “strike while the iron is hot” va yarim aytilgan “don't count your chickens”. E’tibor bering, iboralar orasida oddiy, aniq gaplar ham bor: maslahatning mazmuni iboralarda emas, ular faqat bezak. Sizning javobingizda ham asosiy fikr aniq bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: I love the idea, honestly. But measure twice, cut once: write a proper plan first. And don't burn your bridges at work; you might need that salary for a while. If a real investor appears, then strike while the iron is hot. Until then, don't count your chickens…
scenes.say_uz: G‘oya menga rostdan yoqdi. Lekin yetti o‘lchab, bir kes: avval yaxshi reja yoz. Ishda orqaga yo‘lni yopma, bu maosh senga hali kerak bo‘lishi mumkin. Haqiqiy investor paydo bo‘lsa, temirni qizig‘ida bos. Ungacha jo‘jani kuzda sanaydilar…

scenes.title: Takrorlash: maqol va iboralar
board: Proverbs: same image / different image / no equivalent
Idioms, binomials, similes: fixed form
Flag Uzbek proverbs: As we say in Uzbek…
scenes.say_native: Qisqacha takrorlaymiz. Maqollarning uch turi bor: tasviri ham, ma’nosi ham bir xil; ma’nosi bir, tasviri boshqa; va muqobili yo‘qlari. Iboralar, binomiallar va o‘xshatishlar shaklini o‘zgartirmaydi: artikl va tartib muhim. O‘zbek maqolini keltirsangiz, “As we say in Uzbek” deb belgilang.
scenes.say: Learn each expression as a whole, article and all, and know whether it has an Uzbek twin.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir iborani artikli bilan birga butunligicha o‘rganing va uning o‘zbekcha egizagi bor-yo‘qligini biling.

scenes.title: Takrorlash: kontekst va madaniyat
board: Informal talk ✓ · Academic writing ✗
Half-proverbs sound natural
Sources: Bible · Shakespeare · sea · sport
scenes.say_native: Kontekst: iboralar suhbatda tabiiy, ilmiy va rasmiy matnda emas; og‘ir vaziyatda maqol emas, samimiy gap kerak. Ona tili egalari maqolni ko‘pincha yarmigacha aytadi. Madaniy manbalar: Injil, Shekspir, dengizchilik va sport, Britaniya bilan Amerika farqlari bilan. Eskirgan va aralash iboralardan saqlaning.
scenes.say: Right expression, right moment, right form. That is the whole art of idiomatic English.
scenes.say_uz: To‘g‘ri ibora, to‘g‘ri payt, to‘g‘ri shakl. Idiomatik ingliz tilining butun san’ati shu.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi
board: Use 6 proverbs in context
6 short situations · 1 proverb each · Uzbek equivalent
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: oltita maqolni kontekstda ishlating. Har biri uchun ikki-uch jumlalik kichik vaziyat yozing yoki aytib yozib oling, maqol shu vaziyatning tabiiy qismi bo‘lsin. Yoniga o‘zbekcha muqobilini yoki ma’nosini yozing. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: oltita maqolning shakli xatosiz, kamida bittasi yarmigacha aytilgan va hech biri noo‘rin vaziyatda emas. Keyingi darsda ritorik vositalar va nutq san’atini o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Write six short situations, each with one proverb used naturally, and note its Uzbek equivalent beside it.
scenes.say_uz: Oltita qisqa vaziyat yozing, har birida bitta maqol tabiiy ishlatilsin, yoniga esa uning o‘zbekcha muqobilini yozing.

homework_uz: 6 ta inglizcha maqolni kontekstda ishlating: har biri uchun 2–3 jumlali kichik vaziyat yozing (yoki aytib yozib oling), maqol vaziyatning tabiiy qismi bo‘lsin, yoniga o‘zbekcha muqobili yoki ma’nosini yozing. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: 6 ta maqolning shakli (artikl, so‘z tartibi) xatosiz, kamida bittasi yarmigacha aytilgan va hech biri noo‘rin vaziyatda ishlatilmagan.

quiz.q: Which English proverb matches 'Jo‘jani kuzda sanaydilar'?
options: Don't count your chickens before they're hatched.
The early bird catches the worm.
Birds of a feather flock together.
quiz.why_uz: Ma’no bir xil: natija aniq bo‘lmaguncha xursand bo‘lma. Birinchi variant — so‘zma-so‘z tarjima (calque).

options: It cost an arm and leg.
It cost arm and a leg.
It cost an arm and a leg.
It cost the arm and the leg.
quiz.why_uz: Iborada ikkala artikl ham shart: an arm and a leg.

quiz.q: Which binomial is in the correct order?
quiz.why_uz: Binomiallar tartibi qotgan: salt and pepper, sooner or later, safe and sound, peace and quiet.

quiz.q: 'I'm feeling a bit under the weather.' What does the speaker mean?
quiz.why_uz: “Under the weather” — biroz tobi yo‘q, yengil holsizlik.

quiz.q: Which is the most appropriate in an academic essay?
options: The method is a piece of cake.
The method is as easy as pie.
The method is a walk in the park.
quiz.why_uz: Ilmiy matnda ibora emas, aniq neytral so‘z kerak: straightforward.

quiz.q: A friend walks in just as you mention her name. What do you say?
quiz.why_uz: “Speak of the devil” — “Bo‘ri haqida gapirsang, qulog‘i ko‘rinadi”.

quiz.q: Where does 'the green-eyed monster' (jealousy) come from?

quiz.why_uz: “Learn the ropes” — kemadagi arqonlarni o‘rganishdan; endi “ishning ko‘zini o‘rganmoq”.

quiz.q: 'Qo‘shnining tovug‘i g‘oz ko‘rinar' is closest to…
options: The grass is always greener on the other side.
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
Don't put all your eggs in one basket.
Out of sight, out of mind.
quiz.why_uz: Ikkalasi ham: boshqalarniki doim yaxshiroq ko‘rinadi.

quiz.q: Which sentence contains a mixed idiom?
options: We'll cross that bridge when we come to it.
We'll cross that bridge when we burn it.
It's not my cup of tea.
quiz.why_uz: Ikki ibora aralashgan: cross that bridge when we come to it + burn your bridges.
